about: Which fixture set and systems the headline charts show. Every system and set is in eval/results/index.json, the tables in docs/benchmarks.md and the UI regardless; this only picks what goes on the slide-sized charts. Keys are run-record system.key values.

readme.about: The README's generated blocks (pii-guard eval report rewrites the text between <!-- intro:start --> and <!-- intro:end -->, and between <!-- results:start --> and <!-- results:end -->). Layout 'compact' (LAB-1663): one table with a row per fixture set (columns) and a column per system (rows), each cell 'leak · over-masking', read from each set's latest snapshot in eval/results/runs/. Prose is editorial and lives here; numbers enter it only through placeholders filled from the records: {leak:<set>:<system>}, {over:...}, {partial:...}, {docs:<set>}, {langs:<set>}, {codes:<set>}; a system is a run-record key or an alias. model_latency names the one model-latency measurement the README quotes (LAB-1625's gateway-latency records were taken under heavy load and are too noisy to quote).

model_latency.label: NER model time per message on CPU (the model alone, not the whole gateway)

bullets: **What it does.** An OpenAI-compatible gateway for AI agents: change one base URL, and detected names, addresses, IDs and faces become reversible placeholders (`[[PERSON_7f3a]]`) before the request leaves, then come back in the answer, mid-stream and inside tool calls.

**How well.** On {docs:agent-traffic} fictional agent-traffic documents ({codes:agent-traffic}), {leak:agent-traffic:own} of personal values reached the model and {over:agent-traffic:own} of masks hit text that was not personal data. Same documents and scorer: PrivAiTe {leak:agent-traffic:privaite} / {over:agent-traffic:privaite}, Presidio {leak:agent-traffic:presidio} / {over:agent-traffic:presidio}, LLM Guard {leak:agent-traffic:llm-guard} / {over:agent-traffic:llm-guard}.

**Where your data goes.** In the default fast mode, rules and a small NER model process the original text on your machine. The hosted demo receives what you type, so use fictional data there; the optional audit and SAM 3.1 endpoints receive the original text or pixels. Anything the detectors miss passes through: pseudonymization, not anonymization or a compliance guarantee.

PII Guard fast {leak:agent-traffic:own} leak, {over:agent-traffic:own} over-masking; PrivAiTe {leak:agent-traffic:privaite} and {over:agent-traffic:privaite}; Presidio {leak:agent-traffic:presidio} and {over:agent-traffic:presidio}; LLM Guard {leak:agent-traffic:llm-guard} and {over:agent-traffic:llm-guard}; PII Guard rules only {leak:agent-traffic:rules} and {over:agent-traffic:rules}.
intro.caption: Lower-left is better. {docs:agent-traffic} fictional documents ({codes:agent-traffic}), drawn by pii-guard eval report from the run records. All sets · shareable PNGs

notes: Leak: labeled personal values left fully readable in what the model receives. A value with only part left readable (a surname, the tail of a number) is a partial leak, counted separately: PII Guard fast {partial:agent-traffic:own} on agent traffic, {partial:smoke:own} on the hand-written set. Over-masking: masks on text that was not personal data. Lower is better for both; the lowest in each row is bold.
caveats: The sets are small (tens to hundreds of documents per language): a point or two of difference is noise. Agent traffic is written by Muse models from fictional seeds, which can flatter a detector taught by Muse labels; that is why the hand-written and public sets sit next to it.

Finance text is the weak spot. On Gretel finance's own labels PII Guard leaks {leak:gretel-finance:own}, about level with Presidio's {leak:gretel-finance:presidio}; on corrected labels ([why](docs/datasets.md)) {leak:gretel-finance-corrected:own} against {leak:gretel-finance-corrected:presidio}. Over-masking is high on Gretel finance ({over:gretel-finance:own}) and CEE-PII ({over:cee-pii:own}), where reference numbers without a cue word come out as IDs.

NER v4.2 is behind the previous v2.0 in two places, with the rules in front: CEE-PII {leak:cee-pii:own} against {leak:cee-pii:v20}, and the Polish pl-pii-bench {leak:pl-pii-bench:own} against {leak:pl-pii-bench:v20}. Neither was a release gate; v4.2 won on the hand-written sets, agent traffic and EU languages ([model notes](docs/models.md)).

lines: Every tool ran on the same documents (same fixture hashes) and was scored by the same code; comparison tools use their documented defaults ([configurations](eval/results/2026-10-27-comparison/README.md#systems)). All data is fictional. PII Guard fast is rules plus the published NER `v4.2` ([model card](training/ner/model-card.md)). The hand-written set pools {codes:smoke}; the full tables, per-language numbers, Ai4Privacy (in-distribution for the NER, so not a win) and the corrected finance labels are in [docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md#results-by-fixture-set).

share.about: The shareable images (pii-guard eval report writes docs/benchmarks/<name>[-<size>][-dark].{svg,png}, LAB-1663). Keys are run-record system.key values; names are what the images print, so no candidate ids or ticket ids reach a public image. Every number is read from the run records.
share.claim: Masks personal data before it reaches the LLM, and puts it back in the answer.
